newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 29.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.

- The former Minister for Health, Brendan Howlin, has admitted he did not intervene when he discovered that an expert group he had set up to investigate the Hepatitis C scandal was having trouble getting information from the Blood Transfusion Service Board in 1994.

- The Irish Prime Minister John Bruton has undertaken that he will convey "a general concern" to Judge Gerard Buchanan that the parliamentary inquiry into the Dunnes Stores payments to Irish politicians should get under way shortly.
-Sinn Fein on Tuesday unveiled the elements of its campaign strategy for the British election, linking support for the party with renewed hope for reconstructing the Northern peace process.
- An amendment to the Central Bank Bill 1996 is expected within days to allow the bank to take over the regulation of all investment intermediaries.
- Hopes that the new Partnership 2000 pay deal will be accepted rose significantly on Tuesday night because of support from SIPTU, the country's largest union.
- Health Minister Michael Noonan ran into controversy on Tuesday night over plans to set up a new tribunal of inquiry into infected blood and blood products.

- Deadlock over decommisssioning at the Stormont negotiations on Northern ireland is now almost certain to force talks chairman, Senator George Mitchell to declare his hand by producing a set of compromise proposals.
- More than one in six small and medium sized companies have job vacancies which they cannot fill, according to a survey published on Tuesday.
